results.references:
- Arkadi Nemirovski. [Prox-Method with Rate of Convergence O(1/t) for Variational Inequalities with Lipschitz Continuous Monotone Operators and Smooth Convex-Concave Saddle Point Problems](https://www2.isye.gatech.edu/~nemirovs/SIOPT_MP_2004.pdf). 2004. Complexity: $O(1+LD^2/\varepsilon)$ exact saddle-gradient oracle calls; Mirror-Prox, two calls per iteration, deterministic saddle gap at most $\varepsilon$.
- Axel Böhm, Michael Sedlmayer, Ernö Robert Csetnek, Radu Ioan Boţ. [Two Steps at a Time—Taking GAN Training in Stride with Tseng’s Method](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.09033v1). 2020 preprint, version 1; published 2022. Complexity: $O(1+LD^2/\varepsilon)$ exact saddle-gradient oracle calls for deterministic saddle gap at most $\varepsilon$; forward-backward-forward uses two calls per iteration, and its past-gradient variant uses one per iteration plus one initialization call.

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Minimize in x and maximize in y a differentiable convex-concave function φ over X×Y; no strong convexity or strong concavity is assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query z=(x,y) returns (∇xφ(x,y),−∇yφ(x,y)) exactly. Gradient uniqueness removes dependence on call index and oracle seed; no function values are supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E and F are complete real inner-product spaces, with no finite-dimensional restriction. X and Y are nonempty compact convex sets; the product-domain diameter is at most D≥0. The saddle-gradient map is globally L-Lipschitz, with L>0. All parameters, spaces and constraint sets are public; φ is the hidden instance. The target ε>0 is public. Only oracle calls are budgeted, with fixed cost O(1+LD²/ε); other operations are unrestricted.

accuracy.label: saddle_point_gap
accuracy.details: The measurable output z satisfies E[sup(y∈Y)φ(z.1,y)−inf(x∈X)φ(x,z.2)]≤ε, and this gap is integrable. No last-iterate requirement is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The gap bound is in expectation under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law; deterministic accuracy is not required.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The output belongs to X×Y almost surely; this probability guarantee applies to feasibility.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard smooth convex-concave constrained saddle-point formulation with an exact Lipschitz first-order oracle and expected primal-dual gap accuracy, stated in real Hilbert spaces.
